issues.legal_issue: A pre-emption right attached to land sold can extend to replacement land allotted to the purchaser in consolidation proceedings.
material_facts: Purchasers bought agricultural land that the respondents sought to pre-empt.
Before the suit was filed, consolidation proceedings allotted the purchasers other land in place of the purchased land.
The respondents claimed the land allotted in place of the purchased land, and the pre-emption right remained available at the legally relevant stages.
issues.conclusion: The respondents could enforce their pre-emption right against land allotted to the purchasers in place of the land sold, provided the land was pre-emptible and the right existed at the relevant stages.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the Patiala and East Punjab States Union Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act preserves the rights and obligations attached to the original holding in the land allotted in its place. A pre-emption disability runs with the land, as explained in Shri Audh Behari Singh v. Gajadhar Jaipuria, [1955] 1 S.C.R. 70; Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh, [1959] S.C.R. 878 does not displace that principle, although the ordinary remedial right is to follow the property sold. The pre-emptor must have the right at the date of sale, the date of suit, and the date of decree.

rule.if: preemption_suit and purchased_land_replaced_in_consolidation and preemptor_right_exists_at_required_stages and replacement_land_is_preemptible

predicates.preemption_suit: A claimant brought a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption over land that had been sold.
predicates.purchased_land_replaced_in_consolidation: Consolidation proceedings allotted the purchaser other land in place of the land purchased.
predicates.preemptor_right_exists_at_required_stage: The claimant had the right of pre-emption at the sale, suit, and decree stages.
predicates.replacement_land_is_preemptible: The land allotted in place of the purchased land was subject to a pre-emption right under the applicable law.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption suit concerns purchased land replaced through consolidation, and the right exists at the required stages and applies to the replacement land, the replacement land is subject to pre-emption.

issues.legal_issue: A provision specifically transferring leases, mortgages, or other encumbrances to replacement land does not prevent an inherent ownership disability from continuing on that land.
material_facts: The land sold was replaced by land allotted to the purchasers in consolidation proceedings.
The appellants argued that the separate provision addressing leases, mortgages, and other encumbrances showed that no other obligations continued on replacement land.
The Court treated pre-emption as a disability attached to ownership of the original land.
issues.conclusion: The specific treatment of leases, mortgages, and other encumbrances does not exclude the continuation of an inherent pre-emption disability on replacement land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 preserves the rights and obligations attached to the original holding, including a disability inherent in ownership. Section 25 separately addresses leases, mortgages, and other encumbrances because those do not attach by law to a different parcel in the same way as an incident of ownership. The Court relied on the characterization of pre-emption as a limitation on ownership in Shri Audh Behari Singh v. Gajadhar Jaipuria, [1955] 1 S.C.R. 70.

predicates.consolidation_replaces_owned_land: Consolidation proceedings allot a landowner other land in place of the land originally held.
predicates.original_ownership_has_inherent_disabili: The original land is subject to a disability that attaches to ownership of the land itself.
predicates.replacement_land_takes_place_of_original: The allotted land substitutes for the original land rather than merely receiving a separate contractual encumbrance.

issues.definition: If consolidation replaces land whose ownership carries an inherent disability with substitute land, that disability continues on the substitute land.

issues.legal_issue: The portion of a consolidated allotment attributable to purchased land can be identified even when the allotment also replaces land previously owned by the purchaser.
material_facts: Some purchasers already owned land in the village before buying the land at issue.
Consolidation allotted those purchasers land in blocks in place of both their earlier holdings and the purchased land.
Land was valued for purposes of allotment during consolidation proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The portion of the allotment attributable to the purchased land can be determined by reference to the valuation used in the consolidation proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reasoned that land is valued for purposes of allotment in consolidation proceedings, making it possible to determine how much of a combined allotment corresponds to the land purchased under the sale deed.

predicates.preemption_suit: A claimant brought a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption over land that had been sold.
predicates.consolidated_allotment_replaces_both_pri: A purchaser received a consolidated allotment in place of both previously held land and land acquired by purchase.
predicates.allotment_valuation_was_used: The land was valued in the consolidation process to determine the allotment.

issues.definition: In a pre-emption suit, when a consolidated allotment replaces both earlier holdings and purchased land and the allotment process used valuation, the portion attributable to the purchased land can be identified.

issues.legal_issue: An objection to the form of a decree that was not raised before the High Court need not be entertained for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The appellants objected to the form of the decree before the Supreme Court.
The objection had not been raised in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the objection because it had not been raised in the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural principle that it would not permit a point concerning the form of the decree to be raised for the first time before it when the point had not been raised in the High Court.

predicates.civil_appeal: A party brought a civil appeal from a lower court's judgment and decree.
predicates.decree_form_objection_not_raised_in_high: A party did not raise an objection to the form of the decree before the High Court.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, if a party did not raise an objection to the form of the decree before the High Court, the objection is not entertained.
